free_tier.stated: one free label under any of six live suffixes (bg5.net, is-a.si, nastu.net, tun.re, us.mw, pfsdns.org), resolved on the operator's DNS with A, AAAA, MX, NS, CAA, TXT, CNAME, ALIAS and HTTPS records; no annual fees

per_object_cap.stated: one label under a suffix, never a nested name: myname.is-a.si works and my.name.is-a.si does not; the number of labels per account is not stated on the page read

retention.stated: a domain left empty for 30 consecutive days is reclaimed; no renewal term is stated

interface_detail: a web console at s.eus/domains for search, registration and every record; the earlier pull-request flow has been retired; no record API was read
tooling: the SEUS domain console, then any host that takes a DNS record
chaining: a label with NS records offered in the same console, so delegation to an external DNS service is a record the registrant can set; the suffixes were not found in the captured Public Suffix List, so each name shares one Let's Encrypt count with every user of the suffix

limits.value: a GitHub account at least 2 years old is required, and the account is verified in the console
a domain with no content for 30 consecutive days is reclaimed

identity_cost.detail: an account on the operator's console with a verified GitHub account at least 2 years old; no phone and no card are named on the README

notes: Two binds: the account-age gate, and an operator clock that reclaims an empty name after 30 days, so the owner of the suffix can withdraw it. The zone starts on the operator's DNS, and NS records let the registrant delegate. The TLS limit is a risk here: the suffixes have no entry in the captured Public Suffix List, so each suffix is one registered domain for Let's Encrypt, which is an inference from absence.
